description: Research Experience for Undergraduates (REU), NHERI 2022: Prediction of Peak Pressure Coefficients Using Higher Order Statistics with Machine Learning is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "other", published or maintained by Jennifer Bridge, University of Florida (ufl.edu). This research investigates the prediction of pressure coefficients based on different approach terrain configurations. Machine learning was used to develop an Artificial Neural Network to model these relationships. The data from this project may be used to investigate other relationships that correlate to pressure coefficients. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "other" project. Its DOI is 10.17603/ds2-9dxy-tg94. Keywords: University of Florida Boundary Layer Wind Tunnel, approach terrain configuration, bluff body model, pressure coefficient, machine learning, artificial neural network. Published 2022-08-12. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is CC-BY-4.0 (labelled "Creative Commons Attribution" on the DesignSafe project). Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
